Pain and fever: Relieving pain and reducing fever: non-opioid analgesics, NSAIDs and opioids.
Antibiotics: Drugs that kill or stop the growth of bacteria. They do nothing to viruses.
Antivirals and antifungals: Treating viral and fungal infections, a much smaller toolkit than antibacterials.
Heart and blood pressure: Lowering blood pressure, protecting the heart, and keeping blood flowing without clotting.
Diabetes: Lowering blood sugar, by several different mechanisms.
Mental health: Antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, anxiety and sleep medicines, and stimulants.
Breathing and allergy: Opening the airways, calming inflammation, and blocking allergic reactions.
Stomach and gut: Reducing stomach acid, nausea, and regulating bowel movements.
Thyroid and hormones: Replacing or adjusting hormones, including thyroid treatment and contraception.
Seizures and neurology: Controlling seizures and some other neurological conditions.
Skin, eyes and ears: Topical and local treatments for the skin, eyes and ears.
Immune system and cancer care: Suppressing or redirecting the immune system, and core chemotherapy concepts.
Electrolytes and supplements (prescripti: Correcting deficiencies that go beyond what an over-the-counter multivitamin provides.
